_about: Registry of state and local campaign-finance datasets this connector can query. Each entry was checked against the publisher's live metadata and one live query on the date in verified_on. publisher and publisher_link are copied verbatim from the dataset's own credit (Socrata attribution fields, or the catalogue record named in catalog_record for platforms that carry no credit with the data), never written from memory. Where that credit is a city or portal and not an agency, publisher_is_agency is false and the connector says so. platform is socrata unless stated. A carto or arcgis entry is turned into SQL text, so it may only take integer, enum and present (yes or no) filters. On arcgis the credit is the layer's own copyrightText. An ocpf entry is one fixed list on the Massachusetts OCPF Public API: the year goes in the path, yes/no and listed values go as parameters, and a local filter is only ever compared against the rows that came back. Its credit is read from the API's own description (catalog_record). Every entry carries terms: what the publisher's own pages said about using the data, read on the date given, with the publisher's condition quoted word for word or null when none was found. Re-check with: node tests/verify-jurisdiction-sources.mjs

suggestions.label: Candidate committees with reports this year
Every filer with reports this year, biggest first

notes: Each row is one filer for one calendar year of reports, not a whole campaign. A race that runs across two years has a row for each year, and a candidate can have more than one filer (the candidate personally and a candidate committee). Do not add rows together without saying so.

Totals come from electronic filings only. num_paper_filings counts reports the filer submitted on paper, whose transactions are not in these totals, so a filer with paper filings may have raised or spent more than shown. Per the city's technical documentation.

Office, level, party and district are filled in only where the city matched a filer to its own ballot lists. Many candidate committees have none, most of all outside an election year, so an empty candidate_office does not mean the filer has no race, and filtering by office leaves those filers out. Rows with office_level state are present.
Without a filer_type or candidate_office filter the biggest rows are usually unions and political committees, not candidates.

The city describes these open-data tables as cleaned and enriched for information only, and calls the filing system's raw exports the official record. filer_type was assigned by the city's own review.

ending_unpaid_debts is a balance at the end of the filer's last report that year, so never add it across years. candidate_district_num reads 0 on many rows and the documentation read does not define it, so do not interpret it.
The city's technical documentation says its Board of Ethics and Office of Innovation and Technology developed these tables. That says who built the data, not where any office files.
The catalogue credits the City of Philadelphia and names no agency as publisher. Find the responsible office on the city's own site before naming it.

sources.cycle_filter_reason: Without one the publisher's server cuts the answer off part-way, so the totals shown would not be the biggest.
sources.covers: Election campaign contribution data shared by the Office of Campaign Finance, which the layer's description says is charged with administering and enforcing the District of Columbia laws pertaining to campaign finance operations. The description says it covers contributions reported from 2003 through the current reporting period, is updated daily, and is as reported but may not be complete. It has no office or ward-of-the-race field.
sources.covers_basis: layer description and copyright text, and values observed in live rows

suggestions.label: Committees with a named candidate, this election year

notes: Each row is one committee for one election year, summed from its contribution records. Totals are money received, not net of spending. This connection does not read the separate expenditures table.
The table has no office field, so which race a committee belongs to has to come from elsewhere. Committees with no candidate name are in the data too: set has_candidate to yes to leave them out.
election_year is required. Most records sit in even years; odd years hold few, and a small number of records have no election year and never appear here.
A total of null means the committee's records carry no amounts. The amount field is stored as whole numbers in this layer.
The table also holds each contributor's address and ward. This connection never reads them, so it cannot group by ward.
